body: claimed: agy research (gemini) · 2026-11-15 14:03 UTC · plan: research

**Open question 1, answered: the controller.** mkinney's friend sent the user's manual and wiring diagram of his machine's controller. It is a **RichAuto DSP A11**: a handheld DSP pendant with an interface board, 3-axis, extendable to a 4th (C) axis. Programs run from a USB disk. Source: the RichAuto A11 user's manual (RichAuto S&T, Beijing), summarised here. The manual is not copied into the repo.

What the manual says, relevant to a post:
- It accepts standard G-code and PLT files.
- **The controller has "G-code attribute" settings that change how it reads a program.** A post must match them, or the operator must set them:
  - read or ignore **F** words; read or ignore **S** words; read or ignore **T** words;
  - **arc centres absolute or incremental** (an "absolute centre" on/off switch). This decides how I/J must be written;
  - read or ignore **G54**, **G49** and **G40**;
  - the spindle control mode, a Z filter, and whether the program header is skipped.
- Eight work coordinate systems, switched from the pendant. Power-loss recovery with a breakpoint resume.

Consequences for the sub-issues:
- The post must write arcs in ONE known I/J mode (incremental is the usual default). The test-cut sheet must tell the operator to set "AbsCntr" to match.
- It is safer to make the program work with F, S and T read ON, and not to depend on G54 or G49 (many A11 users ignore them). The work zero is set on the pendant.
- An air cut must confirm the arc direction and size, and the units (G20 or G21).

Next: read the friend's attribute settings from his pendant (a photo of the "Attribute of G code" screen), then file the machine-file, post and test-kit sub-issues.

This comment answers all six open questions on #1907. All facts come from published OEM manuals, RS-274 / ISO 6983 standards, and CamCraft repository files.

---

## 1. Open question 1: the friend's machine

- **Confirmed controller:** RichAuto DSP A11 handheld pendant and interface board. It drives 3 axes and can add a 4th C axis. It reads programs from a USB flash drive. Evidence: RichAuto A11 manual summary in `#issuecomment-6895679726`.
- **Still needed from mkinney and the friend:**
  1. Machine make, model name, and year.
  2. Table X, Y, and Z travel and gantry clearance.
  3. Spindle power, RPM range, collet size (for example ER20, ER25, or ER32), and VFD wiring (8 fixed `S1`-`S8` steps or 0-10 V analog).
  4. Tool changer type (manual collet or ATC) and presence of a 4th C axis.
  5. Photos of the pendant **Attribute of G code** (`G Code Setup`) screen, the version screen, and the Z puck (plus puck thickness in mm).

---

## 2. Open question 2: controllers in these lines

### Laguna Swift line
- **Sizes and types:** `Swift 4x4`, `Swift 4x8`, and `Swift 5x10`. Variants include T-slot, Vacuum, and Multi-Tool (`MT`). Source: Laguna Tools Swift specifications and manuals.
- **Factory controllers:**
  - **RichAuto DSP handheld (HHC):** `A11`, `A11E`, or `B11` (3-axis) on standard Swift routers. Some multi-tool builds use `B18`, `B58`, or `Syntec`.
  - **WinCNC:** PC card controller on earlier `MCNC Swift` machines. Source: Laguna MCNC Swift manual and WinCNC manual.
- **Aftermarket retrofits (not factory stock):** Mach3, Mach4, or UCCNC when owners replace a stock controller.

### Grizzly CNC router line
- `G0403` (Benchtop): **DSP-J2** handheld controller.
- `G0894` (24" x 36"), `G0895` (4' x 8'), and `G0931` / `G0931L` (47" x 47"): **RichAuto DSP A11** handheld controller.
- `G0932` (4' x 8' with rotary 4th axis): **RichAuto DSP B18** handheld controller.
- `G0933` (4' x 8' 4-axis with linear ATC): industrial panel or DSP controller (check machine serial).
- `G0934` (5' x 10' with 8-position rotary ATC): **Siemens Sinumerik 808D Advanced** panel controller.
- Grizzly does not factory-ship Mach3, Mach4, or UCCNC. Source: Grizzly catalog specifications and owner manuals.

### Controller G-code dialects and limits

| Controller | Units and motion | Arcs and planes | Canned cycles | Offsets and TLO | Spindle and M6 | Comments and format | USB and limits |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **RichAuto A11 / B11 / B18** | Internal math uses `mm` (`G21`). Manuals list `G20` and `G21`. Use `G21` to avoid scale errors. Uses `G90` and `G91`. | `G2`/`G3` use `I`/`J`/`K`. Pendant `AbsCntr` sets incremental (`Off`) or absolute (`On`). Control can ignore or reject `G91.1`. `G17` is default (`G18`/`G19` listed). | Manuals list `G80`, `G81`, `G82`, `G83`, `G73`. Base router firmware can reject cycles or `G84`. Plain `G0`/`G1` moves work on all builds. | Menu `Read G54` controls `G54`-`G59`. Pendant stores 8-9 work slots. Manual routers usually set `Ign G49` and `Ign G40`. | `M3`, `M4`, `M5`, and `S` (`Read S`). Many A11 builds wire `S` to 8 fixed speeds (`S1`-`S8`). `G04 P<ms>` dwells in ms. `Read T` controls `M6`; bare `M6` can halt manual machines. `M30` ends. | Use `(...)` comments. Avoid `;`, `%`, and `O` lines (`CodeHead` Skip ignores headers). Use `.nc`, `.tap`, `.mmg`, or `.txt`. | Format USB drive to **FAT16** or **FAT32** (2-8 GB works best). Use **8.3** ASCII filenames with no spaces. Internal flash is 512 MB; copy long files off USB first. |
| **DSP-J2** (`G0403`) | Uses `G20`/`G21`, `G90`/`G91`, `G00`, and `G01`. | Uses `G02`/`G03`. | Expand cycles to `G0`/`G1` moves. | Supports `G54`-`G59`. Operators zero on pendant without `G43`. | Uses `M03`, `M04`, `M05`. Manual `M6` lifts head for bit change. | Use plain **ANSI** text (no UTF-8 BOM). Accepts `(...)` or `;` comments. | Use **FAT16** or **FAT32** USB drive and internal memory. Keep ASCII filenames short. |
| **WinCNC** (earlier Swift) | Uses `G20` (inch) and `G21` or `G22` (mm in older manuals). Uses `G90`, `G91`, and `L91` single-line relative move. | Uses `G02`/`G03` with `I`/`J` or `R`. Supports `G91.1`/`G90.1`. | Supports `G81`, `G83`, `G80`. | `G53` uses machine zero (bare `G53` lifts Z). Uses `G43` and `M37` macros. | Uses `M3` and `M5`. `G4 X<sec>` dwells in seconds (bare `G4` waits for Enter). `M6` runs custom macro. | Use square brackets **`[...]`** for comments. Use `.tap` or `.nc`. | Runs on a local Windows PC with no USB stick limit. |
| **Sinumerik 808D Advanced** (`G0934`) | `G290` Siemens mode (`G710`/`G700`) is default. `G291` on its own line sets ISO mode. | Uses `G2`/`G3` and `G17`/`G18`/`G19`. | Uses `CYCLE81`-`CYCLE84` in `G290`. Uses `G81` in `G291`. | Uses `G54`-`G57`, `G505+`, and `T.. D.. M6` in `G290`. | Uses `S.. M3`, `M5`, and `M2`/`M30`. | Uses `;` comments in `G290` and `(...)` in `G291`. Main files use `.MPF`. | Load `.MPF` via front USB port into CNC part memory. |
| **Mach3 / Mach4 and UCCNC** (retrofits) | Uses `G20`/`G21` and `G90`/`G91`. | Supports `G91.1`/`G90.1` with `I`/`J`/`K` or `R`. | Supports `G81`, `G83`, `G80`. | Uses `G54`-`G59` and `G43 H..` tool tables. | Uses `M3`, `M5`, and `M6` scripts (`.m1s` VB in Mach3; `M6.txt` C# in UCCNC). | Accepts `(...)` or `;`. Uses `.tap`, `.nc`, `.txt`, `.gcode`. | Mach3 demo mode stops at **500 lines**. UCCNC can stop on unknown G-codes. |

## 3. Open question 3: machine data for `.mch` files

Every `.mch` file must follow `docs/MACHINE-ONBOARDING.md`: set `general.vendor` to `"Camcraft"`, omit JSON comments, state `safe_retract`, and set `rigid_tapping` only when OEM sources confirm it. Existing router examples in the repo are `assets/machines/sienci-altmill-4x4.mch` and `assets/machines/tormach-24r.mch`.

| Machine | X x Y cut area | Z travel (clearance) | Rapids (X/Y, Z) | Max cut feed | Spindle and collet | Controller and tool change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Laguna Swift 4x4** | 48" x 48" | ~6"-7.5" stroke (~7"-7.5" gantry) | Up to 900 IPM | 400-600 IPM | 3 HP liquid-cooled, 6,000-24,000 RPM, ER20 | RichAuto DSP (or WinCNC); manual |
| **Laguna Swift 4x8** | 48" x 96" | ~6"-7.5" stroke (~7"-7.5" gantry) | Up to 900 IPM | 400-600 IPM | 3 HP liquid-cooled, 6,000-24,000 RPM, ER20 | RichAuto DSP (or WinCNC); manual |
| **Laguna Swift 5x10** | 60" x 120" | ~6"-7.5" stroke (~7.25"-7.5" gantry) | Up to 900 IPM | 400-600 IPM | 3 HP liquid-cooled, 6,000-24,000 RPM, ER20 | RichAuto DSP (or WinCNC); manual |
| **Grizzly G0894** | 35-3/8" x 23-5/8" | 5" | ~396 IPM X/Y, ~192 IPM Z | <= rapid | 3 HP liquid-cooled, 6,000-24,000 RPM, ER20 | RichAuto A11; manual |
| **Grizzly G0931 / G0931L** | 47-1/4" x 47-1/4" | 6-1/4" to 7-7/8" (manual revision) | ~708-709 IPM X/Y, ~394-396 IPM Z | <= rapid | 3 HP water-cooled, 0-24,000 RPM stated (check VFD min), ER20 | RichAuto A11; manual |
| **Grizzly G0895** | 51" x 98-1/2" | 11" travel (7" clearance) | 1,500 IPM X/Y, 400 IPM Z | <= rapid | 6 HP air-cooled, 6,000-18,000 RPM, ER32 | RichAuto A11; manual |
| **Grizzly G0932** | 51-3/16" x 98-7/16" | 7-7/8" (7-7/8" C swing) | 1,181 IPM X/Y, 400 IPM Z, 472 IPM C | <= rapid | 4 HP HSD air-cooled, 0-18,000 RPM stated, ER25 | RichAuto B18 (4-axis C); manual |
| **Grizzly G0934** | 59-1/16" x 118-1/8" | 7-7/8" | Servo rates (check machine serial) | <= rapid | 12 HP HSD air-cooled, 0-24,000 RPM, ER32 | Sinumerik 808D Advanced; 8-pos rotary ATC |
| **Grizzly G0403** | 15-3/4" x 36" table | ~7-1/16" Z (13" x 25-9/16" travel) | 118 IPM | <= rapid | 68 mm mount (optional 2 HP water-cooled) | DSP-J2; manual |

- **Origin and home conventions:** Machine Z0 sits at the top limit switch (`safe_retract: 0.0`). XY work zero usually sits at the front-left corner of the stock or spoilboard. Z0 work origin sits on the stock top for pocket work, or on the spoilboard top for sheet through-cuts. Manual tool changes happen at a front park position set by the operator.

---

## 4. Open question 4: post needs vs existing CamCraft posts

CamCraft's existing posts (`assets/posts/grblhal.cps`, `fanuc.cps`, `carvera.cps`, `tinyg.cps`, `sinumerik.cps`) already emit `G0`/`G1`/`G2`/`G3`, `F`, `S.. M3`, `M5`, and `M30`. We can also reuse plain-move cycle expansion (`carvera.cps`, `tinyg.cps`) and metric units (`carvera.cps`). No existing post runs safely on a RichAuto DSP A11 without changes:

- **Failures in existing CamCraft posts on RichAuto A11:**
  1. `grblhal.cps` writes `G91.1`, `G94`, `G53 G0 Z...`, `T<n> M6`, and canned cycles `G73`/`G81`/`G82`/`G83`/`G86`/`G89`. RichAuto A11 controls arc centers with `AbsCntr` instead of `G91.1`, can reject `G91.1` or `G53`, and basic A11 firmware can reject canned cycles.
  2. `fanuc.cps` writes `%`, `O0001`, `T.. M6`, `G43 H..`, `G49`, `G91 G28 Z0`, `G28 X0 Y0`, and `G73`/`G81`-`G89`/`G84`. On RichAuto A11, `%` and `O0001` can trigger errors unless `CodeHead = Skip`, `G43`/`G49` depend on `Ign G49`, `M6` can pause or fault manual setups, `G28` depends on controller home setup, and `G84` tapping does not run on these routers.
  3. `tinyg.cps` caps lines at 191 bytes, pauses with `M0` after `T.. M6`, and writes `.gcode` files.
  4. `carvera.cps` targets Makera Carvera machines directly.
- **What the new `richauto.cps` post must do:**
  - **Preamble:** write `G21` (metric `mm` default to prevent `G20` scale errors), `G90`, `G17`, `G40`, and `G80`. Omit `%`, `O` lines, `G91.1`, `G94`, `G43`, `G49`, and `;` comments. Handle `G54` safely (document `Read G54` vs `Ign G54`; refuse `G55`-`G59` or warn cleanly).
  - **Comments:** write short printable ASCII inside parentheses `(...)`.
  - **Spindle and warm-up:** write `S<rpm> M3`. Add an optional dwell property (`G04 P<ms>`) that defaults to `0` when the pendant `Spindle Delay` handles ramp-up. Document `S1`-`S8` discrete step behavior.
  - **Tool changes (`M6`):** refuse mid-program tool changes in the first slice (one tool per `.nc` file), or lift Z and emit `M0` with `(CHANGE TOOL T<n>)`. Avoid bare `T<n> M6` lines that halt `Read T` machines unpredictably.
  - **Drilling and refusals:** expand all drill cycles (`G81`/`G82`/`G83`/`G73`/`G86`/`G89`) to plain `G0`/`G1` moves (`carvera.cps` pattern). Refuse `G84` tapping, `G41`/`G42` cutter compensation, and probing.
  - **End and safe Z:** retract Z to clearance height in work coordinates (no `G91 G28 Z0`), write `M5`, write `M9` if coolant is on, and end with `M30` (no trailing `%`). Use `.nc` extension.
- **Sinumerik 808D (`G0934`):** `assets/posts/sinumerik.cps` writes `G710`/`G700`, `G17`, `G90`, `T.. D.. M6`, `;` comments, `G81`-`G89`, and `M2` with `.nc` extension (`.MPF` header when named). `808D Advanced` needs testing or updates for native `CYCLE81`-`CYCLE84` (`G290`) vs `G291` ISO mode and `.MPF` naming.

---

## 5. Open question 5: operator work flow on RichAuto A11

1. **Power on and home:** Turn on the machine and VFD, release E-stop, and run `All Axes Home` (`Machine Zero`) on the pendant.
2. **Check G Code Setup once:** Open `MENU -> Auto Pro Setup -> G Code Setup`. Set `AbsCntr = Off` (incremental `I`/`J`), `Read F`, and `Read S`. Check `CodeHead`, `Read/Ign T`, `Read/Ign G54`, `Ign G49`, and `Ign G40`. Measure the Z puck with calipers and enter exact mm under `MENU -> Machine Setup -> C.A.D Thickness`.
3. **Prepare the USB drive:** Format a small USB drive (2-8 GB) as **FAT32** (or FAT16). Name `.nc` files with **8.3** ASCII letters and digits with no spaces (for example `TEST1AIR.NC`).
4. **Set work zero (`Origin`):**
   - Clamp test stock and seat the cutter in the collet.
   - Jog X and Y to the stock datum corner and press `ORIGIN` to zero X and Y.
   - Set Z0 on top of the stock: place the Z puck under the bit, attach the ground clip if present, and run auto tool zero (`ON/OFF + MENU` on standard A11). Or touch off manually with paper and zero Z with `ORIGIN`.
5. **Load and run:** Plug the USB drive into the bottom of the pendant, copy long programs into internal memory from `U-Disk`, and run a high air cut before cutting stock.

---

## 6. Open question 6: safe test-cut plan

Use one 1/4" or 6 mm flat end mill for Stages 1 and 2 so no mid-program tool change occurs.

- **Stage 1 — Air cut (`TEST1AIR.NC`, Z0 set 25-50 mm above empty table):**
  - Toolpath: 100 mm x 100 mm square contour plus a 50 mm circle arc pass.
  - Checks: USB load passes with zero errors, `G21` moves exactly 100 mm on screen, `+X`/`+Y`/`+Z` axes move the right way, `G2`/`G3` sweeps a smooth circle (`AbsCntr = Off`), spindle ramps cleanly, and `M30` lifts Z and stops.
- **Stage 2 — Shallow XPS foam or MDF cut (`TEST2CUT.NC`, 2 mm depth, Z0 on stock top):**
  - Toolpath (2D Contour with tabs, 2D Pocket, and plain-move Drill): 100 mm x 100 mm outer square with 4 tabs, one 40 mm round bore pocket, one 30 mm square pocket, and one 6 mm deep hole.
  - Checks: motion is smooth without corner stutter, cut depth matches Z puck `C.A.D Thickness`, and part sizes match `100 mm`, `40 mm` bore, `30 mm` square, and `2 mm`/`6 mm` depths.
- **Stage 3 (optional after Stage 2) — Two-tool pause check:** run an air cut with two separate `.nc` files (`T1`, then `T2`) or test a mid-job manual stop (`M0`) if needed.
- **Report back via mkinney:**
  1. Photos of the `G Code Setup` screen, version screen, and machine spec plate.
  2. Any file load errors or ignored codes, plus how the spindle responds to `S` (`S1`-`S8` steps vs continuous RPM).
  3. Measured X, Y, 40 mm bore diameter (X and Y), and pocket Z depth on the Stage 2 test piece.

---

## Design proposal (smallest useful first slice first)

1. **Slice 1 — `RichAuto DSP A11` post (`assets/posts/richauto.cps`) and goldens:** implement the confirmed controller dialect using `carvera.cps` cycle expansion, `G21` metric units, incremental `I`/`J` (`AbsCntr = Off`), parentheses comments, `M30`, and single-tool / safe-stop rules.
2. **Slice 2 — Machine `.mch` files for Laguna Swift and Grizzly A11 lines plus friend's machine:** follow `docs/MACHINE-ONBOARDING.md` and `sienci-altmill-4x4.mch` / `tormach-24r.mch`, mapping `default_post_for` in `crates/app/src/posting.rs` to `RichAuto DSP A11`.
3. **Slice 3 — Test-cut kit (`docs/tester-kits/richauto-a11-router/`):** commit the `.camproj`, 8.3 `.nc` programs, Rust pin test, and one-page check sheet following `docs/tester-kits/tormach-microarc-4th/`. Update Slices 1-2 if hardware tests show a difference.
4. **Slice 4 — Docs ("Your first router part"):** add the router first-part guide in `site/content/guide/` on the shipped `Sienci AltMill` (`grblHAL`) and include RichAuto A11 shop-router notes.
5. **Slice 5 (deferred `P8`) — Other Laguna and Grizzly controllers:** `WinCNC`, `DSP-J2`, `RichAuto B18` (4-axis C), and `Sinumerik 808D Advanced`, held until Slices 1-3 pass on hardware.

Machine-side sample from the friend's **Laguna Swift** router (2026-11-18), controller **RichAuto DSP A11** (from his manual and pendant photo, firmware `t8-957`): a program his A11 runs, `Dome.mmg` (9,031 lines, a 3D dome finish; made by the CAM he uses today). Only the program's format was read, as evidence of what the A11 accepts; the other CAM product's post-processor file he also sent was **not** opened (clean-room: we never use another CAM's post).

What the controller accepts, from the `.mmg`:
- File extension `.mmg`; ASCII, CRLF line ends; ends with `%`.
- First line a comment `(Filename:  Dome)`, a second comment with the job name later. Comments in parentheses.
- **No spaces between words**: `N60G1Y50.851Z-0.001F1524.0`.
- **Sequence numbers on every block**, `N10`, step 10, up to `N90290` (no wrap at 9999).
- **No setup block**: no G21/G90/G17/G54, no tool change (`T`/`M6`), no length offset - units and modes come from the controller (here mm: XY up to ~101.6, `Z5.080` safe height).
- Spindle on in the first block: `N10M03S11000`; end: `M05`, then `M30`.
- Motion words: `G00` rapid (two digits) and `G1` feed (one digit); `F` in mm/min (`F381.0` plunge, `F1524.0` cut); modal: words that do not change are left out (`G1X50.749Z0.000`).
- Coordinates with three decimals.

This is the dialect for the A11 post, #1914. Still wanted from the owner: travels, spindle range, and later an air cut of a short CamCraft program.

Machine data from the friend's **Laguna Swift + RichAuto DSP A11** (photos of the A11's setup screens, 2026-11-18):

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Machine size (travel), unit mm | **X 1285.000**, **Y 2500.000**, **Z 200.000** (about 50.6" x 98.4" x 7.9") |
| Home speed, unit shown "MMPerSec" | X 3000, Y 3000, Z 1000 (these are the homing speeds, not the cutting/rapid limits; the unit label looks like mm/min in practice - to confirm) |
| Home order | **Z, X, Y** (Z first, then X, then Y) |
| Home direction | X **Neg**, Y **Neg**, Z **Pos** - machine home is at X min, Y min, Z top |

For the machine file (#1914 / a Laguna Swift `.mch`): travels 1285 x 2500 x 200 mm, home at the X-/Y- corner with Z up. Still open: the rapid/feed limits (the A11's speed settings, not the home speeds) and the spindle range (the sample program ran S11000).
